chapter_seo_title: Chapter 275: The Method — Li Huowang Impersonates the Supervisory Heavenly Office
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang bluffs his way into the county yamen, only to be dragged into a humiliating, absurd folk ritual involving bronze gongs and chili powder.
og_title: Li Huowang Impersonates a Government Agent in Chapter 275
og_description: The invisible ghost of Pì County has a bizarre weakness: gong-beating, finger-clamping, and chili powder.
twitter_title: A Very Strange Ritual: Gongs, Clamps, and Chili Powder
twitter_description: Li Huowang's search for answers leads him to an absurdist exorcism that feels more like a trap.

lore_anchors.definition: A government agency under the Ministry of Rites responsible for policing supernatural disasters and rogue cultivators in the Dao-Twisted World. Its name carries terror and authority.
A culture-bound syndrome, also known as Koro, involving the perceived shrinking of the genitals. In the Dao-Twisted World, it is literalized as an attack by an invisible ghost.
The administrative and judicial office of a county magistrate in imperial China. In the Dao-Twisted World, it is a place of hollow authority and often, hidden complicity with horror.
A fictional county in the Dao-Twisted World plagued by the Retracted Yang affliction, its official records suspiciously empty.
A pejorative term for erotic or bawdy Chinese folk opera. In the Dao-Twisted World, it represents a struggling troupe’s last resort for survival.
The traditional Chinese Ghost Festival, held on the 15th day of the 7th lunar month, when the gates of the underworld open and spirits roam the living world.
A face-covering made of threaded old coins; in the Dao-Twisted World, it provides concealment from supernatural perception.
